title: SOMA: A Benchmark for Fine-Grained Egocentric Behavior and Body-Motion Understanding
abstract: arXiv:2610.36384v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Perceiving human body motion is critical for multimodal systems that understand and assist people. Yet current evaluations of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) largely focus on objects, scenes, and coarse actions, leaving their ability to reason about the body itself poorly assessed. This is especially challenging from the egocentric perspective, in which the body is only partially visible and motion must be inferred from occluded and temporally distributed cues. We introduce SOMA, a benchmark for fine-grained body-motion understanding from egocentric video, comprising 1,632 human-verified questions across three capability axes: body configuration, motion dynamics, and temporal reasoning. We evaluate 37 leading closed-source, open-source, and specialized egocentric MLLMs, complemented by an extensive human evaluation. translated_title: SOMA：一个用于细粒度自我中心行为与身体运动理解的基准
translated_abstract: 感知人体运动对于理解和辅助人类的多模态系统至关重要。然而，当前对多模态大语言模型（MLLM）的评估主要集中于物体、场景和粗粒度动作，模型对身体本身进行推理的能力尚未得到充分评估。这从自我中心（第一人称）视角来看尤其具有挑战性，因为在自我中心视角下，身体仅部分可见，运动必须从被遮挡且在时间上分散的线索中推断出来。我们提出了SOMA，一个用于从自我中心视频中理解细粒度身体运动的基准，包含1,632个经人工验证的问题，涵盖三个能力维度：身体构型、运动动态和时间推理。我们评估了37个领先的闭源、开源以及专门针对自我中心的MLLM，并辅以大规模的人类评估。我们发现，仅凭视频完成该任务对人类而言也很困难（准确率为68.5%），但人类的表现仍明显优于（模型）。
tldr: 该论文提出了SOMA基准，通过1,632个经人工验证的问题从身体构型、运动动态和时间推理三个维度评估自我中心视频中的细粒度身体运动理解能力，发现37个领先的MLLM表现不佳，甚至落后于同样认为该任务困难的人类。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces SOMA, a benchmark of 1,632 human-verified questions for fine-grained egocentric body-motion understanding across body configuration, motion dynamics, and temporal reasoning, showing that 37 leading MLLMs perform poorly and fall behind even humans who find the task difficult.
